2. This appeal is filed against the award of the Tribunal in MVC No.1298/2019 dated 16.09.2022 passed by the Court of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'the Tribunal').

sentences.text: 3. One Mahesh aged 6 years met with an accident on 06.11.2018 and his father, as a natural guardian, filed a claim NC: 2025:KHC-K:7102 HC-KAR petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,50,000/-.
The Tribunal considering entire evidence on record, grant an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition till realization.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred in which it is contented that, meager amount is granted under the head pain and suffering.
Though PW2 assessed the disability as 13%, the Tribunal as taken 10%.
Further, the amounts granted under the medical expenses, discomfort and inconvenience are also meager.
Therefore, requested for enhancement.
5. Admittedly, the minor was aged 6 years at the time of the accident.
The appellant has sustained amputation of right great toe and the doctor assessed the disability as 13%.

Hence, in view of citation reported in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in AIR 2014 SC 736, the appellant herein is entitled for Rs.3,00,000/- towards pain and suffering, as the disability is more than 10%.

sentences.text:
Hence, this court NC:
Mahesh vs Hanmanth And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75260200/
2 2025:KHC-K:7102 HC-KAR finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- in view of the guidelines laid down in the above citation supra.
6. The Tribunal granted Rs.13,925/- under medical expenses as per Ex.P9 and Ex.P10 and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.
7.
Appellant was hospitalized for 6 days.
Parents were doing agriculture.

They took care of the boy when he was hospitalized for six days and they might not have attended any other work at least for a period of two months, therefore, considering his notional income as Rs.11,750/-, in view of the fact that accident is of the year 2018, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.23,500/-
(11,750x2) under the head loss of income to the parents.
8. The Tribunal granted Rs.1,00,000/- for loss of amenities and it needs no interference.
9. In all, the total compensation comes to Rs.4,37,425/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7102 HC-KAR 10.
The award passed by the Tribunal is modified as follows:

Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Pain and suffering 3,00,000/-
 2. Loss of amenities 1,00,000/-
 3. Medical expenses 13,925/-
 4. Loss of earning during the laid up period 23,500/-
 for 2 months to his parents
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.4,37,425/- as against Rs.1,20,000/-.

The claimant is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.3,17,425/-.
12.

In the result, the following order is passed:
 i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance company already  deposited the awarded amount of  Rs.1,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal,

therefore, respondent No.2 is directed to  deposit enhanced compensation of Mahesh vs Hanmanth And Anr on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75260200/
3 Rs.3,17,425/- with interest at the rate of 6% within 1 month from the date of this order.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7102 HC-KAR iii)
On such deposit, the appellant/minor child's father is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
